newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pro-European senior French Communist quits party.
newsitem.headline: Pro-European senior French Communist quits party.

text.p: The only prominent supporter of a single European currency in the leadership of France's Communists resigned from the party on Thursday in a dramatic announcement at its renewal congress.
"Comrades, I have come to tell you I am leaving," Philippe Herzog, a politburo economist and member of the European Parliament, told a hushed congress on its second day.
He cited hostility to European economic and monetary union as one of the issues on which the Communists had failed to move with the times.
"The Communist party doesn't have any real programme to transform society," Herzog said.
"It wants to go beyond capitalism, shake things up and attack the power of money, but that's not enough to go into government, manage the country and help the French people to participate in reform."
Herzog was in a tiny minority in the party, isolated over European issues, from a reform faction which intends to stay and give new leader Robert Hue a chance.

Guy Hermier, a leader of the reformers, said the congress was a step towards the greater openness promised by Hue but "the real renewal still has to take place in the transformation of the Communist party and its adaptation to the modern world".

On Wednesday, the Communists began their first congress since the retirement of veteran hardline leader Georges Marchais, seeking to cast off the remains of their Stalinist past and set out a credible left-wing alternative to the opposition Socialist party.

Hue called for a new union of the Left to fight a general election due in March 1998 and, in the case of victory, raised the prospect of Communist ministers joining a Socialist-led government for the first time since 1984.
However, he also acknowledged major differences with the Socialists, notably over a single European currency, on which he has called for a referendum.
